On Mon, Feb 11, 2013 at 5:19 PM, Anna Joy Lehmicke <aleh...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi all,

I'm new to unmarked so I apologize if my question is basic, but I searched through the topics and could find any clarification.

I'm using distsamp to look at point-transect data for Seaside Sparrows. Once I got all the data formatted, I ran null models using half-normal, hazard rate, and uniform key functions just to get myself familiar with the process. When I summarize the models, the AIC value for the uniform is ~400 greater than the other two (1410 vs 1052 and 1059). However, the back-transformed density estimate (which I am interpreting as an average of all point) from the uniform model is much closer to the naive estimate (1.23) than the other two.

Code for the models:
hn_Null <- distsamp(~1~1, umf, keyfun="halfnorm")
haz_Null <- distsamp(~1~1, umf, keyfun="hazard")
uni_Null <- distsamp(~1~1, umf, keyfun="uniform")


Uniform:
Backtransformed linear combination(s) of Density estimate(s)

 Estimate     SE LinComb (Intercept)
     1.09 0.0467    0.09           1

Transformation: exp  

Half-normal:
Backtransformed linear combination(s) of Density estimate(s)

 Estimate    SE LinComb (Intercept)
     3.66 0.246     1.3           1

Transformation: exp 

Hazard-rate:
Backtransformed linear combination(s) of Density estimate(s)

 Estimate    SE LinComb (Intercept)
     3.31 0.283     1.2           1

Transformation: exp


I cannot figure out why the estimates from the uniform model are so different from the other two, and why the estimate from the "worst" model seems to make the most sense. Am I missing something obvious here? I've been banging my head over this all day and any help would be greatly appreciated.
